rationale: Round 1 built and ran correctly, so round 2 escalates obfuscation modestly while respecting that this sample is a floating-point compute benchmark (fbench, whetstone, flops, himenobmtxpa) where hot-loop overhead is the main constraint. SUB stays the workhorse (cheap instruction substitution, near-zero risk), BCF and FLA are raised slightly to add control-flow opacity and diversity in the hot loops, and IBR/ICALL are kept elevated to break static call/branch analysis, with RuntimeCost held around 0.35-0.4 so the selector still hesitates on the most latency-sensitive functions. SPLIT gets a small bump for diversity at negligible cost. IGV remains the most conservative pass since global variable encryption/indirection risks correctness in numeric code with heavy shared state (ReedSolomon, oourafft), and its CorrectnessRisk stays low-weighted to reflect that it is applied only where features clearly favor it. CorrectnessRisk weights are kept at or below 0.2 across all passes to preserve the clean round-1 correctness result.
